immigration-act-1987.s: The Immigration Act 1987 was a New Zealand law that ended the long-standing preference for immigrants from Britain and other traditional source countries. Selection was based instead on skills and personal qualities, regardless of nationality or ethnicity, and a points system…

igboho.s: Igboho is a town in Oyo State, Nigeria, in the north of Yorubaland. In the sixteenth century, after the Nupe drove the Oyo dynasty from Oyo-Ile, it served for several decades as the seat of the exiled Alaafins, and four Alaafins are said to be buried there.

isthmus-of-corinth.s: The Isthmus of Corinth is the narrow strip of land, about 6 kilometres wide at its narrowest, that joins the Peloponnese to mainland Greece. Long fortified against invaders, notably by the Hexamilion wall, it was crossed by the Corinth Canal, completed in 1893.

ibn-muljam.s: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muljam was a Kharijite who assassinated the fourth caliph, Ali ibn Abi Talib, in the mosque of Kufa in January 661, striking him with a poisoned sword during the dawn prayer. The Kharijites had broken with Ali after he accepted arbitration with Muawiya at…

indra.s: Indra is the king of the gods in the Rigveda, the god of thunder and rain who wields the thunderbolt and slays the serpent Vritra to release the waters. He is the most invoked deity of the Vedic hymns.

international-commission-against-impunit.s: The International Commission against Impunity in Guatemala (CICIG) was a United Nations-backed body, set up by agreement with the Guatemalan government, that worked from 2007 to 2019 to investigate criminal networks inside the state. international-railways-of-central-americ.s: International Railways of Central America (IRCA) was a United States-owned railway company formed in 1912 that controlled most of Guatemala's railways as well as lines in El Salvador. indian-institutes-of-technology.s: The Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) are a group of public engineering and technology universities in India, the first founded at Kharagpur in 1951 as part of Jawaharlal Nehru's programme of building scientific and industrial capacity. indira-gandhi.s: Indira Gandhi (1917–1984) was an Indian politician, the daughter of Jawaharlal Nehru, who served as prime minister from 1966 to 1977 and from 1980 until her death, the only woman to hold the office. She nationalised the banks, led India to victory over Pakistan in the war of…

ignalina-nuclear-power-plant.s: The Ignalina Nuclear Power Plant was a Soviet-built nuclear power station at Visaginas in north-eastern Lithuania, with two RBMK reactors of the type used at Chernobyl. Its first reactor began operating in 1983, and at its height it produced most of Lithuania's electricity.

international-petroleum-company.s: The International Petroleum Company was a Canadian-registered subsidiary of Standard Oil of New Jersey that controlled the La Brea y Pariñas oilfields in north-western Peru. illyrian-provinces.s: The Illyrian Provinces were a region of the French Empire created by Napoleon in 1809, after the Treaty of Schönbrunn, from Austrian lands in Carniola, Carinthia, Istria and Croatia together with Dalmatia and Ragusa. With their capital at Ljubljana and governors including…

inkatha-freedom-party.s: The Inkatha Freedom Party is a South African political party founded in 1975 by Mangosuthu Buthelezi as a Zulu cultural and political movement, Inkatha, and relaunched as a party in 1990. Its rivalry with the ANC led to violence in KwaZulu-Natal and the Transvaal townships…

iotorishima.s: Iōtorishima is a small volcanic island at the northern end of the Okinawa Islands, now part of Okinawa Prefecture. Its sulphur was mined for centuries and was one of the Ryukyu Kingdom's few native export goods, sent as tribute to Ming and Qing China, where it was used to make…

issyk-kurgan.s: The Issyk kurgan is a Saka burial mound near the town of Esik, about 50 kilometres east of Almaty in Kazakhstan, excavated in 1969–1970. A side chamber held a young warrior whose clothing and tall pointed headdress were covered with thousands of gold plaques, the so-called…

indo-scythians.s: The Indo-Scythians were Saka groups who moved from Central Asia through Sistan and Gandhara into north-western India from the late second century BCE. Kings such as Maues and Azes I ruled Gandhara and the Punjab in the first century BCE, and Saka satrap dynasties, notably the…

iazyges.s: The Iazyges were a Sarmatian people who settled on the Great Hungarian Plain between the Danube and the Tisza in the early first century CE. They fought Rome under Domitian and in the Marcomannic Wars; after their defeat in 175 Marcus Aurelius sent 5,500 of their horsemen to…

ivailo.s: Ivailo was a swineherd who led a peasant rebellion in north-eastern Bulgaria in 1277 against Mongol raids and the failures of the nobility. He defeated the Mongols, killed Tsar Constantine Tikh in battle and was recognised as tsar, ruling until 1280.

ivan-shishman.s: Ivan Shishman was the last tsar of Bulgaria at Tarnovo, reigning from 1371 to 1395. A son of Ivan Alexander, he inherited a divided realm and became a vassal of the Ottoman sultan Murad I.

icherisheher.s: Icherisheher is the historic walled old city of Baku, Azerbaijan, on the shore of the Caspian Sea. Its streets contain the Maiden Tower, the Palace of the Shirvanshahs, mosques, caravanserais and bathhouses, enclosed by medieval walls.

ichadon.s: Ichadon was a court official of Silla whose martyrdom in 527 led to the kingdom's acceptance of Buddhism. According to tradition he offered to be executed to overcome the opposition of the nobles to the new faith, and when he was beheaded milk-white blood flowed from his neck.

intharacha.s: Intharacha, also known as Nakhon In, was king of Ayutthaya from 1409 to 1424. He had close ties with the Chinese Ming court, which he had visited before his accession.

ince-minareli-madrasa.s: The Ince Minareli Madrasa, the madrasa of the slender minaret, is a Seljuk theological college in Konya, Turkey, built around 1264 for the vizier Sahib Ata Fakhr al-Din Ali. It is famous for its elaborately carved stone portal with bands of inscription.

iranun.s: The Iranun are a people of the coast of Mindanao around Illana Bay in the southern Philippines, with communities also in Sabah. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries Iranun fleets, allied with the Sulu Sultanate, were renowned as maritime raiders, attacking coasts from…

imbokodvo-national-movement.s: The Imbokodvo National Movement was a political party founded in 1964 to represent King Sobhuza II and Swazi traditional authority in the elections that preceded independence. It won every seat in the elections of 1964 and 1967 and governed Swaziland after independence in 1968.

independent-commission-of-experts.s: The Independent Commission of Experts, known as the Bergier Commission, was set up by the Swiss parliament in 1996 and chaired by the historian Jean-François Bergier to investigate Switzerland's role in the Second World War. industrial-and-commercial-workers-union.s: The Industrial and Commercial Workers' Union was a trade union founded by Clements Kadalie in Cape Town in 1919, beginning among dock workers. iran-iraq-war.s: The Iran–Iraq War was fought from September 1980 to August 1988 after Saddam Hussein's Iraq invaded Iran, seeking control of the Shatt al-Arab and hoping to exploit the turmoil of the Iranian Revolution. After early Iraqi gains, Iran recovered its territory by 1982 and the war…

intolerable-acts.s: The Intolerable Acts, called the Coercive Acts in Britain, were four punitive laws passed by the British Parliament in 1774 after the Boston Tea Party. They closed the port of Boston, curtailed self-government in Massachusetts and allowed the quartering of troops, and they…

isaias-medina-angarita.s: Isaías Medina Angarita was a Venezuelan army officer who served as president from 1941 to 1945. intercession-of-the-theotokos.s: The Intercession of the Theotokos (Pokrov) is an Eastern Orthodox feast, celebrated on 1 October (14 October in the Gregorian calendar), commemorating a vision of the Virgin Mary spreading her veil over the faithful in the Blachernae church in Constantinople. ismail-iii.s: Ismail III was a young Safavid prince, Abu Torab, set on the throne of Iran in 1750 by Ali Mardan Khan Bakhtiari and Karim Khan Zand to lend their rule legitimacy. He held no real power: Karim Khan, who ruled as regent (vakil), kept him in confinement, and Ismail III was the…

ica-river.s: The Ica River flows from the Andes to the Pacific through the coastal desert of southern Peru, watering a valley around the city of Ica. Its oasis valley was a centre of the Paracas and Nazca cultures and later of the Ica culture, and it is now known for its vineyards and pisco.

ile-de-la-cite.s: The Île de la Cité is an island in the Seine in the centre of Paris and the oldest core of the city. It is thought to have formed part of Lutetia, the town of the Parisii, and in the Middle Ages it held the royal palace and the cathedral of Notre-Dame, begun in 1163.

iftikhar-ali-khan-pataudi.s: Iftikhar Ali Khan Pataudi was Nawab of Pataudi from 1917 and a cricketer who played Test cricket for both England and India. He scored a century on his Test debut during the Bodyline series in Australia in 1932–33, and in 1946 captained India on its tour of England.

isle-river.s: The Isle is a river of south-western France, about 255 kilometres long, which rises in the Limousin and flows west through the Dordogne department, past Périgueux, to join the Dordogne at Libourne. Its valley was the territory of the Gallic Petrocorii, and Périgueux, their…

ial.s: Iâl, anglicised as Yale, was a medieval commote in north-east Wales, around Llanarmon-yn-Iâl and the Alyn valley. Part of Powys Fadog, it passed after the English conquest to the marcher lordship of Bromfield and Yale.

iuvavum.s: Iuvavum was a Roman town in the province of Noricum on the Salzach, on the site of modern Salzburg in Austria. Raised to a municipium under Emperor Claudius, it declined in the 5th century, and around 696 Saint Rupert founded a church and monastery among its ruins, the origin…

inn-river.s: The Inn is a river of central Europe, flowing about 520 kilometres from the Swiss Engadine through Tyrol and Bavaria to join the Danube at Passau. Its valley, with Innsbruck at its centre, was a main route through the Alps, and the river long carried salt and other goods.

ilanz-articles.s: The Ilanz Articles were two sets of decrees adopted at Ilanz by the Three Leagues of Graubünden in 1524 and 1526. They stripped the bishop of Chur of most of his secular rights, gave the communes control over church appointments and opened the way for the Reformation, making…

ijssel.s: The IJssel is a river of the Netherlands, a branch of the Rhine that leaves it near Arnhem and flows about 125 kilometres north past Zutphen, Deventer and Kampen into the IJsselmeer. In the Middle Ages it was a major trade route, and the Hanseatic towns along its banks became…

idar-oberstein.s: Idar-Oberstein is a town on the Nahe in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, formed in 1933 by joining the towns of Idar and Oberstein. Since the Middle Ages it has been a centre of agate cutting, first using local stones and from the 19th century gemstones imported from Brazil and…

ingush-people.s: The Ingush are a Nakh people of the central North Caucasus, closely related to the Chechens, living mainly in the Republic of Ingushetia in Russia. Organised in clans in mountain villages with stone towers, they adopted Islam largely in the 18th and 19th centuries.

iron-gate-central-asia.s: The Iron Gate is a narrow mountain pass in the Baysun range of southern Uzbekistan, on the route between Samarkand and the Amu Darya. izyaslav-of-polotsk.s: Izyaslav was a son of Vladimir the Great of Kiev and Rogneda of Polotsk, who was granted Polotsk, his mother's homeland, around 987. iona-sysoyevich.s: Iona Sysoyevich was Metropolitan of Rostov from 1652 until his death. He rebuilt the metropolitan's residence in Rostov as a walled ensemble of churches, palaces and towers, now known as the Rostov Kremlin, from the 1670s onwards.

izmit.s: İzmit is a city in north-western Turkey at the head of the Gulf of İzmit on the Sea of Marmara. As ancient Nicomedia it was capital of Bithynia and the eastern residence of Emperor Diocletian.

iziaslav-ii-of-kiev.s: Iziaslav II Mstislavich, a grandson of Vladimir Monomakh, was Grand Prince of Kiev at intervals from 1146 until his death. His reign was dominated by a bitter struggle for Kiev with his uncle Yuri Dolgoruky of Suzdal.

increase-mather.s: Increase Mather was a Puritan minister of Boston's North Church and president of Harvard College from 1685 to 1701. He went to London in 1688 to seek the restoration of Massachusetts's charter and in 1691 obtained a new charter from William III and Mary II, which created the…

international-commission-of-control.s: The International Commission of Control was a body set up by the Great Powers in 1913 to administer newly independent Albania. idumaeans.s: The Idumaeans were the people of Idumaea, the region of southern Judaea and the Negev settled by Edomites from the 6th century BCE. The Hasmonean ruler John Hyrcanus conquered them in the late 2nd century BCE and made them adopt Judaism, and Herod the Great came from an…

ihuatzio.s: Ihuatzio is an archaeological site on the shore of Lake Pátzcuaro in Michoacán, Mexico, one of the three capitals of the Purépecha state. According to the Relación de Michoacán it was ruled by one of Tariacuri's heirs before power was concentrated at Tzintzuntzan.

isabella-ii-of-jerusalem.s: Isabella II, also called Yolande of Brienne, was queen of Jerusalem from 1212 to 1228, inheriting the crown as an infant from her mother Maria of Montferrat. ishhi-addu.s: Ishhi-Addu was king of Qatna in western Syria in the early 18th century BCE, known from the archives of Mari. He allied with Shamshi-Adad I of Upper Mesopotamia and married his daughter to Shamshi-Adad's son Yasmah-Addu, king at Mari.

iban-people.s: The Iban are an indigenous people of Borneo, the largest ethnic group of Sarawak in Malaysia, also living in West Kalimantan and Brunei. Formerly called Sea Dayaks, they were rice farmers living in longhouses and were known for warfare and headhunting, which the Brooke rajahs…

ille-et-vilaine.s: Ille-et-Vilaine is a department of north-western France, in the region of Brittany, named after its two main rivers. It was created in 1790 from part of the old province of Brittany, and its prefecture is Rennes.

irnerius.s: Irnerius was an Italian jurist who taught Roman law at Bologna in the early 12th century and is regarded as the founder of the Bologna school of glossators. His glosses on Justinian's Corpus Juris Civilis revived the systematic study of Roman law, which drew students from all…

ikiza.s: The Ikiza ('the Catastrophe') was a campaign of mass killings in Burundi in 1972, in which the Tutsi-dominated army and the ruling party's youth wing killed perhaps 100,000 to 300,000 Hutu. It followed a Hutu rebellion in the south in April 1972 that had killed thousands of…

iolani-palace.s: ʻIolani Palace in Honolulu was the royal residence of the Kingdom of Hawaii, completed in 1882 for King Kalākaua and lit by electricity from 1887. After the overthrow of the monarchy in 1893 it served as the seat of the provisional government, the Republic of Hawaii and later…

italian-riviera.s: The Italian Riviera is the coastal strip of Liguria in north-western Italy, between the French border and La Spezia, with Genoa at its centre. It is divided into the Riviera di Ponente to the west and the Riviera di Levante to the east.

itaipu-dam.s: The Itaipu Dam is a hydroelectric dam on the Paraná River on the border between Brazil and Paraguay, built jointly by the two countries under a treaty of 1973. Construction began in 1975 and the first turbines went into operation in 1984.

ivan-gundulic.s: Ivan Gundulić was a poet of the Republic of Ragusa (Dubrovnik) and the leading figure of Croatian Baroque literature. His epic Osman celebrates the Polish victory over the Ottomans at Khotyn in 1621, and his pastoral play Dubravka praises the liberty of Ragusa.

ibycus.s: Ibycus was a Greek lyric poet from Rhegion in southern Italy, active in the second half of the 6th century BCE. He spent part of his career at the court of Polycrates, tyrant of Samos, and was counted among the nine canonical lyric poets of ancient Greece.

innocent-of-alaska.s: Innocent of Alaska, born Ivan Veniaminov, was a Russian Orthodox missionary, linguist and bishop. He worked among the Aleut from 1824 and then at Sitka, created a writing system for the Aleut language and translated scripture into it.

imari.s: Imari is a port town in Saga Prefecture on Kyushu, Japan. In the Edo period porcelain made at nearby Arita was shipped from its harbour, so that European buyers called the ware Imari.

ivrea.s: Ivrea is a town in Piedmont, north-western Italy, on the Dora Baltea where it leaves the Alps. Founded by Rome in 100 BCE as the colony of Eporedia to guard the Alpine routes, it was later the seat of the March of Ivrea, whose rulers Berengar II and Arduin became kings of Italy.

ispir.s: İspir is a town in Erzurum province in north-eastern Turkey, on the upper Çoruh river. In the Middle Ages its castle was contested between Georgians, Armenians and Turks; it was held by the Saltukids of Erzurum in the 12th century before passing to the Seljuks of Rum and later…

islahiye.s: İslahiye is a town in Gaziantep province in southern Turkey, in a valley east of the Nur Mountains. Nearby lies the mound of Zincirli, site of ancient Sam'al, an Iron Age kingdom whose palaces and inscriptions have been excavated since the 1880s.

isokelekel.s: Isokelekel is a semi-legendary hero of Pohnpei in Micronesia who, according to oral tradition, overthrew the Saudeleur dynasty. Said to be a son of the thunder god Nahnsapwe, he sailed from Kosrae with a band of warriors, defeated the last Saudeleur at Nan Madol and became the…

irminsul.s: The Irminsul was a sacred pillar, perhaps a great tree trunk, venerated by the pagan Saxons of northern Germany. Frankish annals record that Charlemagne destroyed it in 772, at the start of the Saxon Wars, after capturing the fortress of Eresburg.

ivan-asen-i.s: Ivan Asen I was the co-founder and first ruler of the Second Bulgarian Empire. In 1185, with his brother Theodore-Peter, he led a revolt of Bulgarians and Vlachs against Byzantine taxation at Tarnovo, and after defeating Byzantine armies he was crowned tsar.

ivan-alexander-of-bulgaria.s: Ivan Alexander was tsar of the Second Bulgarian Empire from 1331 to 1371. He made peace with Serbia, recovered lands from Byzantium and presided over a cultural flowering at Tarnovo, including the illuminated Tetraevangelion of 1355–1356 and the Bulgarian translation of the…

ibn-arabi.s: Ibn Arabi was an Andalusian Sufi mystic, philosopher and poet, born in Murcia in 1165, who became one of the most influential thinkers in Islamic history. After years of travel in al-Andalus and the Maghreb he settled in the east and died in Damascus in 1240.

isa-ibn-ali-al-khalifa.s: Isa ibn Ali Al Khalifa was ruler of Bahrain from 1869, when the British installed him after a period of civil war, until 1923. His reign saw Bahrain bound to Britain by the exclusive agreements of 1880 and 1892.

ibbi-sin.s: Ibbi-Sin was the last king of the Third Dynasty of Ur, reigning about 2028–2004 BCE. His reign saw the empire break apart as provinces broke away, Amorite incursions and famine struck, and his official Ishbi-Erra made himself independent at Isin.

ishbi-erra.s: Ishbi-Erra was the founder of the First Dynasty of Isin, ruling about 2017–1985 BCE. An official from Mari in the service of Ibbi-Sin of Ur, he made himself independent at Isin as the Ur III state collapsed.

instructions-of-shuruppak.s: The Instructions of Shuruppak is a Sumerian wisdom text in which Shuruppak, a ruler of the city of that name, gives proverbial advice to his son Ziusudra, the flood hero. Its earliest copies, from Abu Salabikh, date to about 2600–2500 BCE, making it one of the oldest surviving…

iddin-sin.s: Iddin-Sin was a king of Simurrum, a hill kingdom of the Zagros foothills, around the end of the Ur III period, about 2000 BCE. He and his son Zabazuna left inscriptions in Akkadian and a rock relief celebrating victories over their neighbours, which reveal a brief period of…

izium.s: Izium is a city in Kharkiv Oblast in eastern Ukraine, on the Siverskyi Donets river. Founded as a fortress on Muscovy's southern frontier in the 1680s, it became the seat of one of the five Cossack regiments of Sloboda Ukraine.

ionian-university-of-smyrna.s: The Ionian University of Smyrna was a Greek university planned in Smyrna during the Greek administration of the city after 1919. The mathematician Constantin Carathéodory was appointed to organise it in 1920, and buildings, staff and a library were prepared, but it never…

islamic-courts-union.s: The Islamic Courts Union was an alliance of sharia courts in Somalia that took control of Mogadishu in June 2006 after defeating US-backed warlords, bringing a brief period of order to the capital. Its expansion and the rise of hard-line factions provoked an Ethiopian invasion…

ivan-chistyakov.s: Ivan Chistyakov (1900–1979) was a Soviet colonel general who commanded armies at Stalingrad and Kursk during the Second World War. In August 1945 his 25th Army invaded Japanese-held northern Korea from Manchuria and the Soviet Far East, reaching Pyongyang within days.

ibarra.s: Ibarra is a city in northern Ecuador, capital of Imbabura Province, in the Andes north of Quito. Founded by the Spanish in 1606, it was largely rebuilt after an earthquake destroyed it in 1868.

istana-dalam-loka.s: The Istana Dalam Loka is the former royal palace of the sultans of Sumbawa in Sumbawa Besar, on the island of Sumbawa in Indonesia. Built in 1885, it is a large timber building raised on dozens of wooden pillars in the style of local stilt houses.

incwala.s: Incwala is the most important national ceremony of the Swazi Kingdom (Eswatini), held each year around the summer solstice in December and January. Over several weeks the king, regiments and people take part in rites in which the king tastes the first fruits of the harvest,…

ivangorod.s: Ivangorod is a town in Leningrad Oblast, Russia, on the Narva River opposite the Estonian city of Narva. Its fortress was founded in 1492 by Ivan III of Moscow, after whom it is named, facing the Livonian castle across the river.

irrawaddy-river.s: The Irrawaddy, or Ayeyarwady, is the principal river of Myanmar, flowing about 2,170 kilometres from the mountains of the far north to a broad delta on the Andaman Sea. It is the country's main artery of trade and transport, and its dry-zone valley and delta supported the Pyu…

ibn-zaydun.s: Ibn Zaydun (1003–1071) was an Arab poet of Córdoba, regarded as one of the greatest poets of al-Andalus. He served the Jahwarid government of Córdoba but was imprisoned and fled, and later became vizier to the Abbadid kings of Seville, al-Mutadid and al-Mutamid.

ibn-wafid.s: Ibn Wafid (1008–1074) was an Andalusi physician, pharmacologist and agronomist at the court of al-Mamun of Toledo. He wrote a treatise on simple drugs, later translated into Latin, and a work on agriculture.

iapygians.s: The Iapygians were the ancient peoples of Apulia in south-eastern Italy, divided into the Daunians, Peucetians and Messapians, who spoke the Messapic language. They traded and often fought with the Greek colonies of the region, inflicting a heavy defeat on Tarentum and Rhegium…

ixtlilxochitl-i.s: Ixtlilxochitl I was ruler of the Acolhua of Texcoco in the early 15th century. He resisted the Tepanec ruler Tezozomoc of Azcapotzalco and claimed the title of chichimecatecuhtli, but the Tepanecs overran Texcoco and killed him in 1418.

ixtlilxochitl-ii.s: Ixtlilxochitl II was a prince of Texcoco, a son of Nezahualpilli. Passed over for the throne in favour of his brother Cacamatzin in 1516, he rebelled and ruled the northern Acolhua lands, then allied with Hernán Cortés.

intef-i.s: Intef I was a ruler of Thebes in Upper Egypt in the late 22nd century BCE, the first of the Eleventh Dynasty to claim the full titles of a king. Building on the position of his predecessor Mentuhotep I, he asserted royal authority over the southern nomes in rivalry with the…

iuput-high-priest.s: Iuput was an Egyptian prince, a son of Shoshenq I, founder of the Twenty-second Dynasty. Around 943 BCE his father appointed him High Priest of Amun at Thebes, governor of Upper Egypt and army commander, bringing the Theban priesthood under royal control.

iphicrates.s: Iphicrates was an Athenian general known for his use of light-armed peltasts, with which he destroyed a Spartan regiment near Corinth around 390 BCE. He also served abroad as a mercenary commander, leading the Greek troops in the Persian satrap Pharnabazus's failed invasion of…

isis.s: Isis was a major goddess of ancient Egypt, the wife of Osiris and mother of Horus, revered as a protector of kingship, a healer and a model of devoted motherhood. Her cult grew in the Late and Ptolemaic periods, with great temples at Philae and Behbeit el-Hagar, and spread…

iyoas-i.s: Iyoas I was emperor of Ethiopia from 1755 to 1769. Coming to the throne as a boy, he relied on his mother's Oromo relatives, which angered the established nobility.

itagaki-taisuke.s: Itagaki Taisuke was a samurai of the Tosa domain who commanded troops for the new imperial government in the Boshin War of 1868–1869 and served in the early Meiji government. Leaving it in 1873 over a proposed expedition against Korea, he led the Freedom and People's Rights…

ikeda-mitsunaka.s: Ikeda Mitsunaka was a Japanese daimyo who became lord of the Tottori domain in 1632, when as a small child he exchanged his domain of Okayama with his cousin Ikeda Mitsumasa. His line ruled Tottori, covering the provinces of Inaba and Hoki, until the abolition of the domains…

ikeda-nagayoshi.s: Ikeda Nagayoshi was a Japanese daimyo, a younger son of Ikeda Tsuneoki and brother of Ikeda Terumasa. For his service to Tokugawa Ieyasu in the Sekigahara campaign of 1600 he received the small domain of Tottori in Inaba province, which he held until his death.

indutiomarus.s: Indutiomarus was a leader of the Treveri, a Gallic people of the Moselle valley, during Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars. A rival of his son-in-law Cingetorix, who supported Rome, he led the anti-Roman party and in the winter of 54 BCE attacked the camp of Caesar's legate Labienus.

iskar.s: The Iskar is the longest river flowing entirely within Bulgaria, about 370 kilometres long. It rises in the Rila mountains, passes Sofia and cuts a deep gorge through the Balkan Mountains before joining the Danube.

iga-ueno-castle.s: Iga Ueno Castle is a castle in the city of Iga in Mie Prefecture, Japan. First built in the 1580s, it was rebuilt from 1611 by Tōdō Takatora, lord of the Tsu domain, who gave it stone walls about 30 metres high, among the tallest in Japan.

ise-province.s: Ise Province was a province of Japan on the western shore of Ise Bay, now forming most of Mie Prefecture. It contains the Ise Grand Shrine, the most sacred site of Shinto, which drew millions of pilgrims in the Edo period.

ise-grand-shrine.s: The Ise Grand Shrine is a complex of Shinto shrines at Ise in Mie Prefecture, Japan, centred on the Inner Shrine of the sun goddess Amaterasu and the Outer Shrine of Toyouke. Its main sanctuaries are rebuilt every twenty years in the same ancient style.

iroquoian-languages.s: The Iroquoian languages are a family of Native American languages of eastern North America. The northern branch includes the languages of the Five Nations of the Iroquois Confederacy, Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca, together with Tuscarora, Huron-Wendat and…

ivriz-relief.s: The İvriz relief is a rock carving of the 8th century BCE near the village of Aydınkent in Konya Province, Turkey, beside a spring. It shows King Warpalawa of Tuwana worshipping the storm god Tarhunza, who holds a bunch of grapes and ears of wheat.

iuput-ii.s: Iuput II was a king in the Nile Delta in the late 8th century BCE, usually located at Leontopolis and assigned to the Twenty-third Dynasty of Egypt. He was one of the local rulers who joined Tefnakht of Sais and then submitted to the Kushite king Piye during his campaign of…

iguvine-tablets.s: The Iguvine Tablets are seven bronze tablets found at Gubbio, ancient Iguvium, in Umbria in 1444. Written in the Umbrian language, partly in the native Umbrian alphabet and partly in Latin script, between the 3rd and 1st centuries BCE, they record the rites of the Atiedian…

incheon.s: Incheon is a port city on the west coast of South Korea, on the Yellow Sea west of Seoul. Opened to foreign trade as Chemulpo in 1883, it became Korea's main gateway to the capital.

ionian-academy.s: The Ionian Academy was the first Greek institution of higher education of modern times, founded in Corfu in 1824 under British rule by the philhellene Frederick North, 5th Earl of Guilford. Teaching in Greek, it trained a generation of scholars, lawyers and doctors for the…

irkutsk.s: Irkutsk is a city in eastern Siberia, Russia, on the Angara river near Lake Baikal. Founded as a Cossack fort in 1661, it became the administrative centre of eastern Siberia and a hub of trade with China and Mongolia, and many exiled Decembrists settled there.

istaravshan.s: Istaravshan, known until 2000 as Ura-Tyube, is a city in the Sughd region of northern Tajikistan, on the northern slopes of the Turkestan range. One of the oldest towns of Central Asia, it lay in the medieval principality of Ustrushana, whose name the modern city revives.

ibn-al-muqarrab.s: Ibn al-Muqarrab al-Uyuni was an Arabic poet from al-Ahsa in eastern Arabia and a member of the Uyunid ruling family. His diwan, praising and lamenting members of the dynasty and complaining of his own treatment, was later furnished with a long commentary.

islamic-movement-of-uzbekistan.s: The Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan was a militant Islamist group founded in 1998 by Tahir Yuldashev and Juma Namangani with the aim of overthrowing President Islam Karimov. Based in Tajikistan and Afghanistan, it made armed incursions into Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan in 1999 and…

intercatia.s: Intercatia was a town of the Vaccaei in the northern Meseta of Spain, in the region of modern Zamora or Valladolid. In 151 BCE it was besieged by the Roman consul Lucius Licinius Lucullus, and according to ancient writers the young Scipio Aemilianus won a single combat there…

ithaca.s: Ithaca is a small Ionian island off the west coast of Greece, between Cephalonia and the mainland, famed as the home of Odysseus in Homer's Odyssey. After centuries under Byzantine, Norman and Italian lords it passed to Venice around 1500 and shared the history of the Ionian…

itagi.s: Itagi is a village in Koppal district, Karnataka, India, known for the Mahadeva Temple built in 1112 by Mahadeva, a general of the Western Chalukya king Vikramaditya VI. Built in soapstone with richly carved pillars, doorways and tower, the temple is praised in its own…

ivano-frankivsk.s: Ivano-Frankivsk is a city in western Ukraine at the foot of the Carpathians. It was founded in 1662 by the Polish noble Andrzej Potocki as the fortress town of Stanisławów, and passed to Austria with Galicia in 1772.

issyk-kul.s: Issyk-Kul is a large mountain lake without an outlet in north-eastern Kyrgyzstan, lying in the Tian Shan at about 1,600 metres above sea level. Its basin, sheltered pastureland on the routes between the Tarim Basin and the steppe, was home in turn to the Saka, the Wusun, the…

iyo-province.s: Iyo Province was an old province of Japan in north-western Shikoku, corresponding to modern Ehime Prefecture. Under the Tokugawa shogunate it was divided among several domains, among them Matsuyama and Uwajima.

inariyama-sword.s: The Inariyama Sword is an iron sword excavated in 1968 from the Inariyama Kofun in Saitama Prefecture, Japan, whose gold-inlaid inscription was discovered by X-ray in 1978. The text, dated to a year usually read as 471, names the great king Wakatakeru, generally identified…

inle-lake.s: Inle Lake is a freshwater lake in the hills of southern Shan State, Myanmar, at about 880 metres above sea level. It is home to the Intha people, who fish with a distinctive leg-rowing style and grow crops on floating gardens.

intha.s: The Intha are a people living on and around Inle Lake in southern Shan State, Myanmar. Speaking a language close to Burmese, they live in villages of stilt houses, fish by rowing with one leg wrapped around the oar, and farm floating gardens on the lake.

itzamnaaj-bahlam-iii.s: Itzamnaaj B'ahlam III, known as Shield Jaguar the Great, was king of the Maya city of Yaxchilan from 681 to 742. During his long reign the city reached its greatest power, and he commissioned many buildings and carved lintels, among them the lintels of Structure 23 dedicated…

ibrahim-al-hamdi.s: Ibrahim al-Hamdi (1943–1977) was president of the Yemen Arab Republic (North Yemen) from 1974 to 1977. He came to power in a bloodless military coup, curbed the power of the tribal sheikhs, promoted development through local cooperatives and sought closer ties with South Yemen.

ibn-hawshab.s: Ibn Hawshab (died 914), known as Mansur al-Yaman, was the founder of the Isma'ili mission in Yemen. Arriving with Ali ibn al-Fadl around 881, he established a base in the mountains of Maswar north-west of Sanaa, from which missionaries were sent to North Africa, Sind and…

ibn-al-ashath.s: Ibn al-Ash'ath was an Arab nobleman of Kufa who led a great revolt against the Umayyad governor al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf from 700 to 703. Sent with a large army against the Zunbils of southern Afghanistan, he turned it against al-Hajjaj and marched on Iraq, winning wide support.

isthmus-of-tehuantepec.s: The Isthmus of Tehuantepec is the narrowest part of Mexico, about 200 kilometres wide, between the Gulf of Mexico and the Pacific Ocean in the states of Oaxaca and Veracruz. Long a corridor for trade between central Mexico and Central America, it was conquered by the Zapotecs…

italian-war-of-1551-1559.s: The Italian War of 1551–1559 was the last of the Italian Wars, fought between Henry II of France and the Habsburgs, Charles V and then Philip II of Spain, with England joining Spain in 1557. After Spanish victories at St Quentin (1557) and Gravelines (1558) and the French…

imjin-war.s: The Imjin War was the invasion of Korea by Japan under Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1592 and again in 1597. Japanese armies quickly took Seoul and Pyongyang, but Korean resistance, the navy of Admiral Yi Sun-sin and a large Ming Chinese intervention halted them; the Japanese withdrew…

invasion-of-the-waikato.s: The Invasion of the Waikato was the largest campaign of the New Zealand Wars, fought in 1863–1864 by British and colonial forces against the Māori King Movement in the Waikato region of the North Island. After battles at Rangiriri and Ōrākau the King Movement withdrew south,…

italian-war-of-1521-1526.s: The Italian War of 1521–1526 was fought between Francis I of France and Emperor Charles V, allied with Henry VIII of England and the papacy, mainly over the Duchy of Milan. After French defeats at Bicocca (1522) and the Sesia (1524), Francis was captured at Pavia in 1525 and…

ikhwan-revolt.s: The Ikhwan revolt was an uprising of the Ikhwan, the Wahhabi tribal militia that had helped Ibn Saud conquer Arabia, against his authority. Led by Faisal al-Dawish and others, they objected to modern innovations and his ban on raids into British-protected Iraq and Kuwait.

irish-confederate-wars.s: The Irish Confederate Wars were the Irish part of the Wars of the Three Kingdoms, beginning with the Irish Rebellion of 1641. Catholic Confederate Ireland, governed from Kilkenny, fought English and Scottish Protestant forces and the royalists in a complex war.

indo-pakistani-war-of-1965.s: The Indo-Pakistani War of 1965 was fought between India and Pakistan from August to September 1965. It began with Operation Gibraltar, an attempt by Pakistan to infiltrate fighters into Jammu and Kashmir, and widened into large tank battles in Punjab.

italian-war-of-1499-1504.s: The Italian War of 1499–1504 was fought by Louis XII of France, who conquered the Duchy of Milan in 1499 and then shared the Kingdom of Naples with Ferdinand of Aragon. The partners fell out, and the Spanish general Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeated the French at Cerignola…

ingrian-war.s: The Ingrian War was fought between Sweden and the Tsardom of Russia during and after Russia's Time of Troubles. Swedish troops occupied Novgorod in 1611, and Sweden supported a Swedish candidate for the Russian throne.
